record.original_question: Does every bridgeless cubic graph have six perfect matchings whose multiset union covers each edge exactly twice?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.5 Every bridgeless cubic graph has a collection of six perfect matchings that together contain each edge exactly twice.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A graph is called cubic if every vertex has degree exactly 3, and bridgeless if it contains no edge whose removal disconnects the graph. A perfect matching of a graph G is a set of edges M ⊆ E(G) such that every vertex of G is incident with exactly one edge of M. A multiset {M_1, M_2, …, M_k} of perfect matchings is said to cover each edge exactly twice if, for every edge e ∈ E(G), the number of indices i ∈ {1, …, k} with e ∈ M_i is exactly 2.

Prove or disprove: For every bridgeless cubic graph G, there exists a multiset of six perfect matchings M_1, …, M_6 of G such that each edge of G belongs to exactly two of the matchings (counted with multiplicity).
artifact.category_tag: Berge-Fulkerson conjecture / perfect matchings in cubic graphs
artifact.status_search_result: The Berge-Fulkerson conjecture remains open as of 2025-2026. It is trivial for 3-edge-colourable cubic graphs but unresolved in general, with recent partial results establishing it for various families of snarks (e.g., cubic graphs with small colouring defect, certain classes of snarks) and for oriented variants on specific families.
